cards.explanation: The answer is in the assembly of the godly. The psalm says, "Sing to the LORD a new song—His praise in the assembly of the godly." So this song isn't a solo in the shower. It's a gathering of people praising Him together. Bring your voice, friends, even if it cracks. (Psalm 149:1)

The answer is True. Psalm 149:3 says, "Let them praise His name with dancing…" Dancing is right there in the text. The psalm puts it first, before the tambourine and harp. I'd give it a hop myself, friends.

The reason is that the LORD takes pleasure in His people. Psalm 149:4 says, "For the LORD takes pleasure in His people…" Read that one slowly, friends. He's not just putting up with them. He takes pleasure in them, and that's why the dancing and the music make sense.
The answer is False. Psalm 149:4 says, "He adorns the afflicted with salvation." No riches in that verse, friends. It's salvation, and I'd trade a drawer full of gold for that any day.

The answer is the saints. Psalm 149:5 says, "Let the saints exult in glory; let them shout for joy upon their beds." So the shouting for joy is for them. Joy gets a loud voice here, friends, and I like it.

The answer is a double-edged sword. Psalm 149:6 says, "May the high praises of God be in their mouths, and a double-edged sword in their hands…" Praise in the mouth and a sword in the hand, side by side. It's a heavy picture, friends, and the next verses say what the sword is for.

The answer is True, and it's a heavy line. The psalm says the sword is "…to inflict vengeance on the nations and punishment on the peoples…" (Psalm 149:7). It's right there in the text, friends. I think this one is worth sitting with for a moment.

The answer is kings. Psalm 149:8 says, "…to bind their kings with chains and their nobles with shackles of iron…" Kings in chains and nobles in iron shackles. It's a hard picture, friends, so take it slowly.

The answer is the judgment written against them. Psalm 149:9 says, "…to execute the judgment written against them." The psalm calls it a judgment that is written, friends. It's a heavy line, so I'll leave it right there.
